findings.what: A public screenshot shows the first name "David" in the Decisions screen's question line ("What did David decide...").
findings.why: Privacy hygiene, not blocking on a docs node. It is the app's own on-screen text and not a path, email or key. David should confirm that a first name in a public repo is acceptable. PR note only.

notes: Scope: I judged delta.patch (b1253d2..HEAD) only. It touches docs/specs, docs/guides/ui, UI_UserGuide.pdf and trail files, and no src/ or tests/.
API1, API2, API5: n/a, auth and roles are out of scope. API7: n/a, no outbound fetching in src/, and the diff changes no src/. API10: n/a, no upstream APIs.
API3, API4, API6, API8 and API9 are marked covered because the diff has no server code, DTOs, SQL, packages or logging for them to reach. Nothing in the guide weakens any of them.

NET extras: no raw SQL, no money type changes, no package changes and no secrets in the diff. A grep of the text files in docs/guides/ui and of the spec found no drive-letter or /Users or /home paths, no emails, no "nagro", no keys and no private-key blocks. The only hits were localhost URLs, which are fine.

capture.mjs: no child_process, exec or spawn. Its only network calls are fetch of <app-url>/trace.json and the browser driving that app URL, and the app URL is a CLI or env argument. The Playwright path comes from PLAYWRIGHT_MODULE or repo-relative candidates. Output paths are derived from import.meta.url. It writes only to docs/guides/ui/shots. The run suffix keeps its test data to its own references.

build.mjs: no shelling out and no network. It reads WEB_SRC, which the header says is read only and never written into the output, plus the manifest and run-output.json. It writes only index.html. It HTML-escapes every extracted code line and manifest string through esc(). The remaining unescaped insertions come from literals in the script itself, so they are not an injection path.

index.html: it has no script tags, no external origin, and no file:// or absolute path. Its only links are repo-relative, and the style sheet is ../assets/guide.css. The PDF has no local-path, file:///, email or "nagro" byte hits. I could not inspect compressed PDF streams. The orchestrator's gate reports the PDF bytes free of local paths, so I rely on that for the compressed content.

Screenshots: I viewed ex-session.png and ex-decisions.png and the others were not opened. The first shows a Not found page, and the host or any path appears nowhere on it. I did not open the remaining 36 PNGs. The gate and the compiler's privacy denylist (DATA-5) cover them.

The guide's instructions are safe. Every command is local: npm ci/build/preview, dotnet run, curl to localhost, the Postman CLI and Playwright. It tells the reader to update visual baselines only deliberately. It tells no one to disable a check, to run anything remote or to use credentials. The Static Web App is described as evidence only, never deployed.

Non-security observation for the PR: the guide's "One session snapshot" shot (ex-session) captured a Not found page, not a snapshot. The text under it describes a snapshot view. The builder's disclosed gaps (the renew success path, commands shown without output, one dark shot, four untagged regions) are noted and not security issues.
